title: Record Heatwaves Put Pressure on Europe’s Energy and Safety
subtitle: Extreme temperatures continue to disrupt power supplies and threaten lives across central and eastern Europe.

summary.en: Central and eastern Europe are experiencing record-breaking heat that is causing serious problems for energy systems. Power plants have been forced to shut down because water levels in rivers are too low for cooling. Thousands of people have died due to the extreme weather conditions this summer. Officials are asking citizens to reduce electricity use while activists call for faster action on climate change. The situation highlights the growing risks that extreme heat poses to infrastructure and public health.
summary.zh: 中歐與東歐正經歷破紀錄的高溫，對能源系統造成嚴重問題。由於河流水位過低無法進行冷卻，發電廠被迫關閉。今年夏天，極端天氣已導致數千人死亡。官員呼籲民眾減少用電，而運動人士則要求針對氣候變遷採取更迅速的行動。此情況凸顯了極端高溫對基礎設施與公共衛生日益增加的風險。

paragraphs.en: Central and eastern Europe are currently facing a period of extreme heat that has broken temperature records across multiple countries. This weather event is part of a longer, difficult summer that has caused widespread droughts and wildfires. As temperatures continue to rise, the region is dealing with the dangerous consequences of a changing climate, which is putting significant pressure on both energy systems and the safety of local populations.
paragraphs.zh: 中歐與東歐目前正經歷一段極端高溫期，多國氣溫紛紛打破紀錄。這波天氣現象是漫長且艱困夏季的一部分，已導致廣泛的乾旱與野火。隨著氣溫持續攀升，該地區正承受氣候變遷帶來的危險後果，這對能源系統與當地民眾的安全都造成了巨大壓力。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, several countries have recently registered their highest temperatures ever. In Slovakia, officials reported a new record high of 42 degrees Celsius in the town of Dolné Plachtince. Austria also saw record heat, reaching 41.2 degrees Celsius. These high temperatures are not just uncomfortable; they are causing major disruptions to critical infrastructure, specifically the power plants that provide electricity to millions of people.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》報導，多個國家近期測得史上最高溫。在斯洛伐克，官員通報多爾內普拉赫廷采鎮（Dolné Plachtince）創下攝氏四十二度的新高紀錄。奧地利也出現破紀錄高溫，達到攝氏四十一點二度。這些高溫不僅讓人感到不適，更對關鍵基礎設施造成嚴重干擾，特別是為數百萬人提供電力的發電廠。

paragraphs.en: One of the most serious problems is the lack of water needed to keep power plants running. Many power stations rely on water from rivers to cool their equipment. When river levels drop too low because of drought, these plants cannot operate safely. In Poland, authorities were forced to shut down the Kozienice and Połaniec coal-fired power plants because the Vistula River did not have enough water to cool them. This shutdown removed a large amount of electricity capacity from the Polish power system, creating a difficult situation for the country’s energy security.
paragraphs.zh: 最嚴重的問題之一是缺乏維持發電廠運作所需的水源。許多發電站仰賴河水來冷卻設備。當乾旱導致河流水位過低時，這些電廠便無法安全運作。在波蘭，當局被迫關閉科傑尼采（Kozienice）與波瓦涅茨（Połaniec）燃煤發電廠，因為維斯瓦河（Vistula River）的水量不足以進行冷卻。這次關閉導致波蘭電力系統損失了大量發電容量，使該國的能源安全陷入困境。

paragraphs.en: Similar issues have affected other parts of the region. In Hungary, the Paks nuclear power plant had to be temporarily powered down due to low water levels in the Danube River. While the Hungarian prime minister, Péter Magyar, recently announced that one of the plant's turbines is back in operation, he warned that the country still needs to reduce electricity consumption. He noted that while water levels in the Danube have risen slightly, the situation remains fragile and dependent on future rainfall.
paragraphs.zh: 類似的問題也影響了該地區的其他地方。在匈牙利，帕克什（Paks）核電廠因多瑙河（Danube River）水位過低而被迫暫時降載。雖然匈牙利總理馬札爾（Péter Magyar）近期宣布該廠其中一部渦輪機已恢復運作，但他警告該國仍需減少電力消耗。他指出，儘管多瑙河水位略有回升，但情況依然脆弱，且取決於未來的降雨量。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the energy sector, the human cost of this summer has been severe. The Robert Koch Institute in Germany estimates that approximately 11,900 people have died from heat-related causes across the country this summer. These figures have led to protests and calls for government action. In Germany, climate activists gathered outside the chancellery to demand an end to the use of fossil fuels. Annkatrin Schwirten, a representative from the group Fridays for Future Berlin, described the current situation as a result of irresponsible energy policies. She argued that society must not accept thousands of heat-related deaths as a normal part of every summer.
paragraphs.zh: 除了能源部門，這個夏天的人命損失也相當慘重。德國羅伯特·柯霍研究所（Robert Koch Institute）估計，今年夏天全德國約有一萬一千九百人死於高溫相關原因。這些數據引發了抗議活動，並呼籲政府採取行動。在德國，氣候運動人士聚集在總理府外，要求終止使用化石燃料。「未來星期五（Fridays for Future）」柏林分部的代表施維爾滕（Annkatrin Schwirten）形容目前的情況是不負責任的能源政策所導致的結果。她主張，社會絕不能將數千人因高溫死亡視為每年夏天的常態。

paragraphs.en: Environmental experts are also highlighting the connection between energy production and the climate crisis. Paweł Pomian, from the Polish environmental organisation EKO-UNIA, stated that power plants that contribute to climate change are increasingly becoming its victims. He suggested that the current crisis should serve as a wake-up call for all of Europe. According to Pomian, shifting toward wind and solar power is essential because these technologies require very little water to generate electricity, which would help protect both energy supplies and river ecosystems.
paragraphs.zh: 環境專家也強調了能源生產與氣候危機之間的關聯。波蘭環保組織「EKO-UNIA」的波米安（Paweł Pomian）表示，造成氣候變遷的發電廠正日益成為氣候變遷的受害者。他認為目前的危機應對全歐洲敲響警鐘。根據波米安的說法，轉向風能與太陽能至關重要，因為這些技術發電時幾乎不需要用水，這將有助於保護能源供應與河流生態系統。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the dry and hot conditions have created a high risk of wildfires across the continent. Data from the European Forest Fire Information System shows that about half a million hectares of land have burned across the European Union since the beginning of the year. Countries like Spain and France have been hit particularly hard, and a large area has also burned in Ukraine. The combination of heat, lack of rain, and strong winds makes it much harder for firefighters to control these blazes. In Austria, officials reported that the conditions for fires are currently more than twice as severe as any previous record for this time of year.
paragraphs.zh: 同時，乾燥與炎熱的氣候已在歐洲大陸造成極高的野火風險。根據歐洲森林火災資訊系統的數據顯示，自今年年初以來，歐盟境內已有約五十萬公頃的土地被燒毀。西班牙與法國等國受創尤深，烏克蘭也有大片土地遭火焚。高溫、缺乏降雨與強風的綜合影響，使得消防人員更難以控制火勢。奧地利官員通報，目前的火災條件比往年同期任何紀錄都嚴重兩倍以上。

paragraphs.en: As the heatwave continues, the outlook remains uncertain. Governments are taking steps to manage the immediate crisis, such as the Polish prime minister’s request for employers to provide air conditioning and cold water for their staff. However, the long-term challenge of protecting people and infrastructure from such extreme weather is becoming more urgent. With climate experts warning that these events are becoming more frequent, the pressure on European nations to adapt their energy systems and improve public safety measures is likely to grow in the coming years.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著熱浪持續，前景依然不明朗。各國政府正採取措施應對眼前的危機，例如波蘭總理要求雇主為員工提供空調與冷水。然而，保護民眾與基礎設施免受此類極端天氣影響的長期挑戰正變得日益迫切。隨著氣候專家警告這類事件發生的頻率正不斷增加，歐洲各國在未來幾年內，調整能源系統與改善公共安全措施的壓力勢必會持續升高。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To turn off or reduce the operation of a machine or system.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 關閉或降低機器、系統的運作。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於電子產品（關機），這裡指發電廠降低運作。文中：In Hungary, the Paks nuclear power plant had to be temporarily powered down due to low water levels in the Danube River.

keyTerms.definitionEn: An event that warns people that they need to change their behavior or take action.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 警訊；敲響警鐘（提醒人們必須採取行動）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「叫醒電話」，這裡指引發警覺的事件。文中：He suggested that the current crisis should serve as a wake-up call for all of Europe.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be affected by something negative, such as a disaster or crisis.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「打擊」，這裡指地區受到災害影響。文中：Countries like Spain and France have been hit particularly hard, and a large area has also burned in Ukraine.

The Danube River has reached record-low levels, making it difficult to cool nuclear power plants. Hungary and Romania are the most affected countries, with both forced to reduce their energy output. Large companies in Hungary have been asked to save electricity to manage the shortage. Experts warn that the situation will likely continue for several weeks.

quiz.question: According to the article, why were the Kozienice and Połaniec power plants in Poland shut down?

options.A: The plants were damaged by severe wildfires in the surrounding area.
options.B: The Vistula River's water levels were too low to effectively cool the plant's equipment.
options.C: The government ordered a mandatory reduction in electricity consumption across the country.
options.D: The plants were being converted to run on wind and solar energy instead of coal.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確提到，波蘭的 Kozienice 和 Połaniec 發電廠被迫關閉，是因為維斯瓦河（Vistula River）的水位過低，無法提供足夠的水來冷卻設備。選項 A 雖然文章其他段落提到野火，但非關閉原因；選項 C 是匈牙利的狀況；選項 D 文中並未提及這兩座電廠正在轉換能源。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between traditional power plants and the current climate crisis?

options.A: Traditional power plants are immune to the effects of climate change due to their advanced cooling systems.
options.B: The crisis is forcing governments to abandon all forms of electricity production during the summer.
options.C: The reliance on water-dependent power plants makes energy systems vulnerable to the very climate change these plants help cause.
options.D: Wind and solar power plants are currently the primary cause of the extreme heatwaves in Europe.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段 Paweł Pomian 的觀點，傳統發電廠（如燃煤或核能）不僅導致氣候變遷，同時也成為氣候變遷的受害者，因為它們依賴水資源來運作，而氣候變遷導致的乾旱正好威脅到此運作模式。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 過度誇大，政府僅是採取節能或暫時關閉措施；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到風能與太陽能是解決方案而非成因。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'fragile' mean as it is used to describe the energy situation in Hungary?

options.A: Easily damaged or likely to fail if conditions worsen.
options.B: Extremely expensive to maintain during the summer months.
options.C: Completely resolved and no longer a cause for concern.
options.D: Highly efficient and capable of handling future heatwaves.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到匈牙利核電廠雖部分恢復運作，但總理警告情況依然「fragile」，且依賴未來的降雨，這代表局勢不穩，隨時可能因氣候惡化而中斷。選項 B 文中未提成本；選項 C 與文意相反，情況仍需警惕；選項 D 則與「fragile」的負面含義完全不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the current heatwave in Europe?

options.A: The heatwave is primarily a local issue affecting only the power infrastructure of Eastern Europe.
options.B: Climate change is creating a cycle of extreme weather that threatens both human safety and critical energy infrastructure.
options.C: The most effective way to combat the heat is to increase the use of fossil fuels to power more air conditioning units.
options.D: European governments have successfully solved the energy crisis by implementing new water conservation policies.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文綜合討論了熱浪對能源系統（電廠冷卻問題）、公共安全（死亡人數）及環境（野火）的廣泛影響，並指出這與氣候變遷有直接關聯，強調了適應與轉型的必要性。選項 A 忽略了對人命的影響；選項 C 與環保人士的訴求背道而馳；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到挑戰依然嚴峻且長期。
